correctness.rationale: For finite G, each nonempty level-pair stratum of a reflexive product-compatible relation on E2 x G is a subgroup of G x G; containing the diagonal makes it H_N for a unique normal N. Compatibility gives normal N=K11<=M=K00 and independent optional normal cross strata X,Y between N and M. The sixteen stratum products are compatible under these inclusions. Congruences have both X,Y empty or N=M=X=Y. Hence D=Σ_{N<=M}(1+I(N,M))² and C=|N(G)|+#normal subgroup interval pairs. For elementary abelian rank d, Gaussian binomial intervals give log_p D=d²/2+O(log d) and log_p C=d²/3+O(log d), so log_p χ/d² -> -1/6 for fixed p. Independently enumerated all compatible reflexive relations for G=C2 (17) and compared with the formula; original checker additionally exhausts trivial,C3,C2xC2 but those runs were not independently reproduced. There is no general arbitrary-group assertion based solely on small enumeration.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge PASS for all compatible reflexive relations of two-level direct-product Clifford monoids and exact fixed-prime rank-decay law. Barber–Ruškuc explicitly construct only an injection of a family of diagonal subsemigroups for arbitrary Clifford semigroups and state it need not be exhaustive; their bound χ(S)<=χ(E(S)) is much weaker. Classical congruence pairs cover the congruence portion but not all compatible non-equivalence relations or the full numerator/denominator count.
residual_risks: Older compatible-relation classifications for strong semilattices of groups could imply this two-level identity-map specialization.
The p^-d²/6 asymptotic holds for fixed p and d increasing only; infinite groups/nonidentity connecting maps are outside scope.

value.rationale: The DSC coefficient is the natural probability of a random compatible reflexive relation being a congruence. An exact normal-lattice classification and a sharp p^(-d²/6+o(d²)) decay for a canonical two-level Clifford family resolve meaningful enumerative and asymptotic questions.
